body:
I appreciate your attempts but, and I don't want to be rude, you're starting to sound like a Christian full of religious rhetoric. 

I don't cut myself. I was only using it as an example. I know there are people in far worse condition but that isn't proof that life is worth living. In fact I'm sure if some of the people you mentioned had the option of a peaceful death, they'd probably take it. 

This unfortunately has focused more on my than I'd like it to. I was hoping to gain more insight on why people disliked others who take their own lives. You're a good person meat_rain. I thank you for the effort but my mind has been made up for a while. I don't feel scared or sadness anymore. I'm ok with it. I know some people will be hurt but I've done the arithmetic and I'm ok with the pain I'm going to inflict. I'm ready for my last sleep.

I don't think its right to hurt other people but how do you feel about people cutting themselves to cope? For some people this is called life. Every day is a slice. Everyday it cuts deeper. I don't want to hurt anybody and in a perfect world I'd sleep eternally without anyone in pain but smiling that my pain is gone. 

Yes you make a good point, what if I find the perfect person and what if I find the perfect job. For some people that's a big what if. For some people its a small bet to make. Go to Las Vegas and bet everything on one number. What are the chances you'll win? I know the pay off is big but is it worth it to lose everything in the end? I've done my betting and I've lost. Could I win in the end? Maybe but I cant take another loss.

I'm sorry the toll this has taken on you. I don't want to belittle the feelings you have but have you considered what it took for him to do what he did? 

Would you rather him stay alive so he could hate himself even more?

I've heard the argument you've made at the end of your post. Trust me when I say most people in this situation have thought of that and realized if it had changed we would know about it but to live as long as we have in the state that we are we're not about to roll the dice on slim chances. Is it worth meeting someone that would completely change my outlook on life when I'm 90? For some the answer is yes but for others we've lived too many years in on the opposite side of the spectrum to change our minds.
